open_points.subject: 00_product.md:Decisions: Decisions — changed since its latest review.
open_points.text: Until the second release the owner meets the review's purpose by hand, from the governance's schedule.
open_points.question: What exact first-release procedure, inputs and observable result let the owner identify every customer and archived project due for action, and what happens if the governance schedule is still draft, missing or ambiguous?
options: Use the provisional periods in R0-94 and inspect Registry records manually
Require an approved governance schedule before performing the review
Defer action whenever the schedule has no final applicable period
open_points.default_guess: Use the currently documented governance period, inspect all ended customers and archived projects manually, and record any unresolved schedule rule for governance review.

witness.initial: The first release is running; a project was archived long enough ago to be due under the provisional five-year period, but the legal review has not finalized the governance schedule.
events: The owner performs the periodic review without the R0-94 review page.
outcomes: The owner applies the provisional period and anonymises or deletes the project.
The owner treats the draft as non-operative and leaves the project unchanged.
witness.observer: The owner and anyone whose data remains in the project

open_points.subject: 00_product.md:Decisions: Decisions — changed since its latest review.
open_points.text: the infrastructure, to which they are ordinary HTTPS, sees only what it sees of its own
open_points.question: Which infrastructure components exist, what request or connection facts each observes or records, how long those facts remain, and whether any of them are available to the owner?
options: No infrastructure component retains a usable observation
A proxy or server records ordinary HTTP metadata and status codes but cannot classify Registry's reason for refusal
Network infrastructure records only connection metadata
Infrastructure observations vary by deployment and Registry makes no guarantee about them
open_points.default_guess: Registry relies on no infrastructure telemetry; any incidental connection or HTTP metadata is deployment-specific and cannot classify these attempts.

open_points.subject: 00_product.md:Decisions: Decisions — changed since its latest review.
open_points.text: closing it is what the second release's counters are for
open_points.question: Does “closing” promise that the owner will eventually see every counted attempt, or only attempts still present in the current process lifetime when the owner next signs in?
options: Best-effort visibility since the latest restart, as R0-97's in-memory counters imply
Durable visibility of every attempt until the owner acknowledges it
Visibility may be lost on restart, but a lost interval must be shown explicitly after sign-in
open_points.default_guess: Treat the counters as best-effort visibility for the current process lifetime and state that restarts can erase unseen attempts.

witness.initial: The second release is running with empty in-memory counters and the owner is signed out.
events: A caller uses an unknown token and Registry refuses the call.
Registry restarts before the owner signs in.
The owner signs in and sees the counters page.
outcomes: The gap is considered closed only if the owner is told that the attempt occurred.
The restart-cleared counters show no attempt, so the owner remains unaware.
